A.why: A green box helm on a green-and-black body reads too close to fenscale, with little bronze or bone and no single strong outline from above.
A.fix: Make bronze the main colour with moss growing on it, and turn the cube great-helm into a crowned or crested regal shape.

B.why: The bronze post-crown helm is a clear, regal idea from above, but the near-black boxy body reads like dark iron and drops bone entirely.
B.fix: Turn the bronze trim into bronze plates, add a bone accent and a face guard, and enlarge and break up the crown posts.

C.why: The slung round grave-shield on the back is a distinctive silhouette, but the striped brown tunic reads as leather and the cap reads as a hat.
C.fix: Shift the tunic from brown to verdigris bronze, enlarge the back roundel, and give the helm a guard or crown rim plus some bone.

D.why: A bone-tined crown helm, one moss-grown pauldron and all four brief colours give the most readable, on-brief barrow-guard.
D.fix: Warm the grey cuirass to tarnished bronze so it stops echoing iron, and roughen the crown tines.

E.why: The wide moss mantle and the tabard-and-greaves lower body give a strong outline, but the tan body risks reading as linen and the mantle overhangs the arms.
E.fix: Darken the hauberk to green-bronze, rag or rim the mantle edge so it is not a plain slab, and seat it closer to the shoulder.

F.why: The horned black helm reads as a raider and pulls towards the Reaver family, and the horns are lost from the overhead camera.
F.fix: Replace the horns with a tall bronze crest or crown that reads from above, and cut the thin chest banding into fewer, bolder bands.

notes: Judged from software renders only (sheet.png plus the six per-letter sheets, at normal and slim fit). D is the only set that lands bronze, moss, bone and black together around a regal crown idea. E has the strongest outline but its colour drifts towards linen. B's and D's crowns are the best helm ideas in the batch. Common problems: bone is missing in B and C, there is too much flat green (A, E), and parts are spent on thin bands that cannot be read from the ARPG camera.
